newsitem.title: CHINA: HK stocks seen lifted by Dow, but advance limited.
newsitem.headline: HK stocks seen lifted by Dow, but advance limited.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks could stage a modest rebound on Wednesday, lifted by positive sentiment generated by Wall Street, but brokers said uncertainties in the political arena would keep most buyers sidelined.
"The market could open high but then turn down under selling pressure," said a broker with a large local house. "Buyers are staying on the sidelines waiting for political developments."
The Hang Seng Index closed 66.41 points, or 0.45 percent, lower at 14,792.17 on Tuesday on turnover of HK$17.57 billion.
Overnight, the Dow industrials jumped 103.82 points, or 1.32 percent, to 7,962.31.

The reason for the Dow's surge -- better second quarter earnings for U.S. companies -- was not directly beneficial to Hong Kong, but brokers said the Hang Seng should undergo a technical rebound after the declines of the past week.
"It should be a cautious, technical rebound," said Allen Pao, in institutional sales at South China Securities.
On Tuesday, the index closed just above its 20-day moving average at 14,687, but below its 10-day, a weak signal.
The market is uncertain how Hong Kong's new government is going to handle critical issues such as election procedures, land supply and illegal immigration, brokers said.
